_comment: usb_id -> @model crosswalk. usb_id is the small integer POD Go reports over USB for a block (a MessagePack uint decoded from each occupied slot section, right after the constant 'c2 19' prefix, before the '1aff09' marker). The DECODE RULE is hardware-confirmed on two independent captures (3/3 cross-checks held: Vol 224, Amp DelSol 289, EQ Parametric 472 re-read identically); amps and cabs use the same encoding. This MAP is still PARTIAL (10 of 574 models) and is built empirically -- see 'derivation' below for why, and how to complete it.
derivation: The usb_id -> @model table is NOT in POD Go Edit: the app (x86-64, unstripped, ~45.6k symbols) decompiles clean of any static table -- no catalog field, no array in any model order, no string- or FNV-hash-keyed map; it keeps blocks as numeric ids at runtime and gets them from the unit. usb_id is the Helix/HX platform's GLOBAL model id, assigned in firmware-introduction order -- so it is NOT the PodGoModelDefs.bin array index (refuted: Deluxe Comp is 99, not index 193) and no single flat catalog ordering reproduces it, BUT (corrects the earlier 'not derivable from any ordering') it is strictly MONOTONIC with PodGoModelDefs.bin order WITHIN each numeric category. Full coverage: capture POD Go Edit fetching the device's model list(s) -- browse every block's model picker once, connected -- then align to catalog order with tools/decode_model_list.py. Details: docs/reference/usb-id-mapping.md.
decode: within an occupied slot section (slot_type 0x06), find 'c2 19', then read a msgpack uint (fixint <0x80, 0xcc=uint8, 0xcd=uint16 BE); that value is the usb_id. It sits immediately before the '1aff09' marker.
source_captures: USBIDCAL2 (capture 2): vol/trem/autoswell-comp/amp/eq/cab (6 blocks, none dropped) - cross-checks 224/289/472 held
